description: Defines the organizational level at which the parent workflow should be analyzed. This field tells the agent what organizational boundary should be treated as the main analysis frame: a single local unit, the whole organization, a network of related organizations, or a process that crosses independent organizational boundaries. It is used to decide whether surrounding activities should be considered internal to the parent workflow, upstream, downstream, adjacent, or external.

allowed_values.meaning: The workflow should be analyzed within one specific local operational unit, such as a department, ward, office, branch, team, or service unit.
allowed_values.use_when: Use this when the user wants to focus on how the workflow works inside one local unit, even if other departments or organizations are involved around it.
allowed_values.boundary_effect: Activities performed outside the selected local unit may be treated as upstream, downstream, adjacent, or external to the parent workflow, even if they belong to the same larger organization.
allowed_values.example: Analyzing patient discharge only inside one hospital ward.

allowed_values.meaning: The workflow should be analyzed within the boundary of one entire organization.
allowed_values.use_when: Use this when the workflow may involve multiple internal departments, units, or teams, but all of them belong to the same organization.
allowed_values.boundary_effect: Activities performed by different internal departments may still be considered part of the parent workflow if they contribute directly to the same organizational process.
allowed_values.example: Analyzing the discharge workflow across the whole hospital, including ward staff, pharmacy, administration, and social services if they are internal.

allowed_values.meaning: The workflow should be analyzed within a network or group of related organizations that operate under the same parent group, healthcare network, corporate group, or shared governance structure.
allowed_values.use_when: Use this when the workflow involves multiple related organizations that are not the same local unit but are still part of a broader coordinated network.
allowed_values.boundary_effect: Activities across different entities in the same network may be considered internal or semi-internal depending on their operational relationship to the parent workflow.
allowed_values.example: Analyzing a patient transfer workflow between hospitals belonging to the same healthcare network.

allowed_values.meaning: The workflow should be analyzed as a process that crosses boundaries between independent organizations.
allowed_values.use_when: Use this when the parent workflow intentionally includes coordination between separate organizations, such as a hospital, public authority, insurance company, external provider, municipality, or third-party service.
allowed_values.boundary_effect: External organizational interactions may be included inside the parent workflow if they are essential parts of the process being analyzed, rather than automatically treated as outside dependencies.
allowed_values.example: Analyzing hospital discharge planning that includes the hospital, municipality, external care provider, and family doctor.

allowed_values.meaning: The intended organizational analysis boundary is not yet known or cannot be determined from the input.
allowed_values.use_when: Use this when the user has not specified whether the workflow should be analyzed at local-unit, whole-organization, network, or cross-organization level.
allowed_values.boundary_effect: The agent should avoid making a strong assumption and should surface this as a boundary uncertainty or ask a confirmation question.
allowed_values.example: The user describes a workflow but does not clarify whether only one department or the whole organization should be included.
